title: A long weekend in Chicago, for two people who read buildings
variant: Magazine spread per day: a numbered rail beside a narrative
prompt: A long weekend in Chicago for two people who love architecture.
note: Magazine register: a serif title, each day as a two-column spread with the places numbered in walking order on the left rail and a narrative on the right, so the rail is both the places list and the map, and the narrative can read as prose with no repeated addresses. Evenings are one italic line each, the glance is a ruled band rather than a card strip, and the page is airy with hairlines and no photos, because the reader is planning at a desk and the buildings are the pictures.
